title: Distinguish batch validity, relational schema and metadata propagation
brief: Arrow Schema/Field describe physical arrays and metadata; DFSchema adds relational qualifiers. Batch construction validates structural contracts, not application meaning. Test metadata through the exact operator path.

choices.tradeoff: Zero-column rows need explicit row count; domain validation is separate.
Do not discard qualifiers before resolution when names collide.

choices.choose_when: Adapt physical expressions to table/file schema differences
choices.tradeoff: Inspect missing-column, casting and nested-field policy; not arbitrary domain schema migration.

claims.statement: RecordBatch::try_new checks field/column count, datatypes and row lengths, including top-level non-nullable fields. It does not validate domain units, keys or every semantic invariant.
Extension annotations reside in field metadata. Direct filter preserves the tested field/schema metadata; that does not prove UNION, projection, cast or custom UDF paths preserve it.
Schema alignment must account for field order, type, nullability and nested structure, not only names. DFSchema qualifiers and physical Schema are different representations.

implementation: Specify which metadata is contractual versus advisory.
Carry or reconstruct fields explicitly when kernels return only arrays.
Probe each consequential logical-to-physical operator boundary, including schema plus values.
unknowns: Nested metadata propagation and every adapter conversion remain contract-backed discovery, not an exhaustive runtime matrix.

evidence.scope: Pinned hosted rustdoc; availability depends on the consumer profile.
Only the named assertions in the recorded Cargo profile.

invalidation.reason: Review changed signatures, docs, availability, and newly viable alternatives.
